raw_move: learn normal and abnormal prompts with auxiliary anomaly data
naive_story: we do prompt learning for normal and abnormal classes
packaging: object-agnostic prompt learning for generic normality and abnormality
constructed_problem: object semantics in CLIP prompts can distract from abnormality/normality and hurt transfer to unseen objects
transfer_pattern: remove a misleading conditioning variable and reframe the method as learning task-level evidence

raw_move: condition prompts on image features in a CoCoOp-like way and refine text embeddings with dense visual features
naive_story: we use visual-conditioned prompts for ZSAS
packaging: visual context prompting when product categories are unknown
constructed_problem: fixed or product-specific prompts are brittle because the category and visual context of unseen products are not available as clean text
transfer_pattern: turn an unavailable variable into a visual-context surrogate

raw_move: add residual adapters to text and image encoders and train them in two stages
packaging: make CLIP anomaly-aware by first learning anomaly-aware text anchors and then aligning patch features
constructed_problem: CLIP has anomaly-unawareness: normal and abnormal semantics are entangled and patch-text alignment is vague
transfer_pattern: turn fine-tuning into concept acquisition followed by representation alignment

raw_move: use prompt ensembles and window-level CLIP features
naive_story: we ensemble prompts and slide windows
packaging: language defines normal/anomalous states and window features provide local evidence
constructed_problem: CLIP works for object recognition but anomaly states are contextual and local
transfer_pattern: convert prompt engineering into state definition plus local evidence extraction

raw_move: add static and dynamic learnable prompts to CLIP encoders
naive_story: we use both CoOp-style and CoCoOp-style prompts
packaging: hybrid prompts combine shared anomaly adaptation with instance-specific adaptation
constructed_problem: static prompts are stable but under-adaptive; dynamic prompts are flexible but insufficient alone
transfer_pattern: split one adaptation problem into stable global memory and dynamic local response

raw_move: use LLM-generated anomaly descriptions, learnable templates, GroundingDINO coarse boxes, and multi-scale patch interaction
naive_story: we enrich prompts with LLM descriptions and improve localization with detector boxes
constructed_problem: generic anomaly words miss category-specific defect semantics, and patch-text similarity creates background false positives
transfer_pattern: turn external tools into expert knowledge and coarse-to-fine evidence refinement

raw_move: learn prompts from normal samples using semantic concatenation and explicit margin
naive_story: we adapt prompt learning to few-shot anomaly detection
packaging: one-class prompt learning with synthetic negative prompt semantics
constructed_problem: contrastive prompt learning needs negative classes, but only normal images are available
transfer_pattern: manufacture the missing contrast in representation space rather than collecting missing data

raw_move: inject frequency cues, reorder channels, apply spectral projection, compare to anchors
naive_story: we add frequency-domain modules to ZSAD
packaging: frequency-deviation anchoring in a source-derived channel-spectral space
constructed_problem: spatial features and text references underuse subtle frequency-dependent deviations; anomalies are not always high-frequency
transfer_pattern: replace a single-cue assumption with structured multi-cue evidence

raw_move: update prompts at test time using augmented views and entropy minimization
packaging: single-test-sample prompt tuning that retrieves CLIP knowledge without training data
constructed_problem: hand prompts are brittle and prompt tuning normally needs downstream data; at inference only one unlabeled sample is available
transfer_pattern: turn test-time optimization into adaptive context retrieval under a data-absence constraint

raw_move: relax OT marginal constraints and solve with entropic scaling
naive_story: we use a relaxed OT loss
packaging: unbalanced transport handles mass variation and partial correspondence
constructed_problem: classical matching assumes all mass must match, which is wrong when evidence is missing, partial, or unmatched
transfer_pattern: relax an unrealistic conservation constraint and present the method as partial evidence matching

raw_move: embed data in hyperbolic space instead of Euclidean space
naive_story: we replace Euclidean features with hyperbolic features
packaging: negative-curvature geometry compactly captures hierarchy and similarity
constructed_problem: Euclidean spaces need high dimensionality for tree-like or hierarchical structure
transfer_pattern: change geometry only when the data story is hierarchy, scale, or entailment

raw_move: apply wavelet, scattering, DCT, or frequency decomposition before attention, matching, or anomaly scoring
naive_story: we add a wavelet or frequency branch
packaging: multiscale stable evidence for subtle local anomaly deviations
constructed_problem: single spatial or semantic representations can smooth away weak scale-frequency defects, while pure frequency statistics lose locality
transfer_pattern: turn frequency features into structured multiscale evidence rather than a generic extra branch
